A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DETRPose, with matching core components, equations, and benchmarks. All main-text and appendix pages were readable, including figures and tables, supporting comparison despite substantial rewriting and expansion.

before.justification: V1 reports original DETRPose results on COCO and CrowdPose, latency measurements, and component ablations, including COCO validation results in Appendix A.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical results and adds OCHuman evaluation, expanded ablations, convergence analyses, NMS experiments, and reduced-query/depth evaluations.

M1.justification: The denoising, FDR, Pose-LQE, and KSVF core remains. V2 adds DETRPose† inference variants that remove queries and later decoder layers without retraining (Section 4.5 and Appendix D). It also explicitly describes projection-layer removal, although the PDFs do not establish whether that optimization is new or newly documented.

E1.justification: V2 adds COCO-trained evaluation on OCHuman, extending coverage to a distinct occlusion-heavy distribution-shift scenario. Appendix B also evaluates object detection alongside pose estimation when studying NMS. COCO validation coverage already existed in v1's appendix and is not a new benchmark.

E2.justification: V2 adds YOLO26 comparisons and introduces YOLO-Pose, ED-Pose, and GroupPose into the COCO validation comparison. Conversely, its COCO test-dev table removes DirectPose, FCPose, CID, InsPose, CenterNet, and RTMO-R50; its CrowdPose table removes PETR and QueryPose. V1's ED-Pose† is matched to v2's ED-Pose-Swin-L-5S rather than counted as newly added.

E3.justification: V1's 12-epoch sequential ablation becomes a fully trained component-combination study with FDR already included in the baseline. Reported CrowdPose training schedules change, including DETRPose-S from 150 to 156 epochs and X from 80 to 48. V2 moves latency benchmarking to an RTX A5500 and adds FP32 comparisons, NMS confidence-threshold controls, and inference configuration sweeps.

E4.justification: V2 substantially expands analysis beyond v1's sequential component additions. Tables 6–8 test component interactions, alternative pretraining, dependence on keypoint constants and segmentation areas, and query/depth tradeoffs. OCHuman robustness tests, NMS sensitivity experiments, and convergence curves add evidence about generalization, latency, and training mechanisms.

E5.justification: V2 newly specifies median latency aggregation through the Roboflow benchmarking tool (Section 4.3); v1 leaves aggregation unspecified. Neither version reports training seeds, repeated-training counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: V2 adds substantial OCHuman, ablation, convergence, and modified-inference results. Existing HGNet-based COCO test-dev AP values remain unchanged, but COCO validation DETRPose-L AP changes from 72.5 to 72.7, and CrowdPose-S AP_H changes from 5.93 to 59.3. Parameter and latency entries also change extensively; the different benchmarking hardware prevents interpreting latency differences as same-setting speedups.

T1.justification: Section 3.1 revises the denoising scale definition from a normalized quantity to human segmented area bounded by image area. V2's Equation 4 removes the extra wh factor appearing under the square root in v1, making it consistent with Equation 3, and explicitly defines the CrowdPose bounding-box-area proxy. These are localized mathematical corrections and definitions.

C1.justification: The first-real-time-transformer claim and four principal component contributions remain. V2 adds out-of-distribution robustness as a headline claim and more specific efficiency comparisons. V1's explicit claim of competitive inference without quantization libraries is dropped, while v2 foregrounds TensorRT FP16 measurements.

C2.justification: V2 adds interpretations concerning component synergy, pretraining effects, annotation requirements, capacity-dependent inference reductions, and possible overfitting by larger OCHuman baselines. It omits v1's explicit tracking and keypoint-visibility limitations. The transpose-related latency limitation is retained in the conclusion, with stronger causal attribution to group attention.

D1.justification: V2 supplies important previously missing details: 100 positive and 100 negative denoising queries, attention-mask direction, area estimation, KSVF constants, backbone-specific learning rates, augmentation details, and comparator letterboxing with padding masks. Appendix A documents RTMO's pretraining configuration. The code link remains, but v1's explicit TensorRT version numbers are no longer supplied.

R1.justification: V2 adds a focused denoising-related-work subsection and citations covering spatial queries, localization-quality estimation, VarifocalNet, segmentation resources, OCHuman, and YOLO26; CenterNet is removed. These clarify attribution and update the comparison context while retaining the central positioning as a GroupPose/D-FINE-based real-time pose estimator.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, related work, and method explanations are extensively rewritten. Results are reorganized into datasets, variants, implementation, comparisons, and expanded analysis; COCO validation moves into the main text. The appendices are restructured, and the retained latency limitation moves into the conclusion.

P2.justification: V2 changes the page template and substantially redesigns the evidence presentation: comparison tables gain resource and training columns, the sequential ablation becomes a component matrix, and new convergence and cross-dataset plots appear. The architecture and Pose-LQE drawings are largely relocated, while denoising panels are reordered and captions revised.

improvement.justification: Full-training component/pretraining ablations, explicit implementation details, and OCHuman testing improve support and reproducibility relative to v1's short sequential ablation. The net gain is limited by reporting inconsistencies and omitted limitations. For example, v2 Section 4.4 claims DETRPose-X surpasses all COCO validation comparators, but Table 3 reports 73.3 AP versus 75.7 for ED-Pose-Swin-L-5S. V1's explicit tracking and visibility caveats also disappear.
